problem: Reversing the weights before delegating and reversing the result afterwards makes tied remainders go to the highest index instead of the lowest, so allocate('0.01',[1,1]) now returns [0.00, 0.01] instead of main's [0.01, 0.00].

list(weights) now runs before places and amount are validated, so invalid arguments raise a different exception type than on main (e.g. allocate(10, None, places=-1) raises TypeError instead of ValueError) and a weights iterable is consumed before validation.

Because weights are validated in reversed order, the last invalid weight rather than the first is reported, which changes the exception type (e.g. [0.5, 0] raises ValueError instead of main's TypeError).

Production code now depends at runtime on reference_impl, a copy of main's allocate.py, which makes any comparison against the reference self-referential and ties the real implementation to a module named as a reference.
Fraction is no longer used (ruff F401 fails) and _to_decimal (lines 6-13) is dead code left over from the rework.
